q: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and _____.
e: All samples of matter can be divided into two categories: pure substances and mixtures. A mixture holds substances together physically, and its composition can vary. Compounds would fill a different blank than mixtures.

q: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant _____.
e: A pure substance is a form of matter that always has a definite and constant composition. Composition is the idea that completes this fact. Volume would fill a different blank than composition.

q: At the beginning of the 19th century, _____ proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms.
e: At the beginning of the 19th century, John Dalton proposed the theory of matter: that all matter was composed of atoms. Dalton treated atoms as the tiny particles that make up elements. Albert Einstein would fill a different blank than John Dalton.

q: Elements are substances consisting of _____ type of atom.
e: Elements are substances consisting of one type of atom. One is the idea that completes this fact. Two would fill a different blank than one.

q: There are _____ known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined state.
e: There are 92 known elements which occur naturally, either in the free or combined state. 92 is the idea that completes this fact. 82 would fill a different blank than 92.

q: Metals show metallic luster, whereas non-metals do not show metallic _____.
e: Metals show metallic luster, whereas non-metals do not show metallic luster. Luster is the idea that completes this fact. Conductivity is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Most of the metals are malleable and ductile, while non-metals are usually _____.
e: Most of the metals are malleable and ductile, while non-metals are usually brittle. Brittle is the idea that completes this fact. Ductile would fill a different blank than brittle.

q: A molecule of an element consists of atoms of the _____ kind.
e: A molecule of an element consists of atoms of the same kind. Same is the idea that completes this fact. Multiple would fill a different blank than same.

q: A molecule of a compound consists of more than _____ kind of atoms.
e: A molecule of a compound consists of more than one kind of atoms. One is the idea that completes this fact. Two would fill a different blank than one.

q: A hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a _____ molecule.
e: A hydrogen molecule is formed by two atoms of hydrogen, so it is a diatomic molecule. Diatomic is the idea that completes this fact. Polyatomic would fill a different blank than diatomic.

q: Water is formed by combining two different elements, so it is a triatomic molecule or a _____ compound.
e: Water is formed by combining two different elements, so it is a triatomic molecule or a binary compound. Binary is the idea that completes this fact. Quaternary would fill a different blank than binary.

q: Ethanol is a polyatomic molecule formed from three different elements, so it is a _____ compound.
e: Ethanol is a polyatomic molecule formed from three different elements, so it is a ternary compound. Ternary is the idea that completes this fact. Quaternary would fill a different blank than ternary.

q: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not _____ combined.
e: Mixtures consist of two or more different substances that are mixed physically but not chemically combined. Chemically is the idea that completes this fact. Gravitationally is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Brass is a solid-solid _____ mixture of the elements copper and zinc.
e: Brass is a solid-solid homogeneous mixture of the elements copper and zinc. A homogeneous mixture looks the same throughout, like a clear solution. Colloidal would fill a different blank than homogeneous.

q: A mixture of flour and rice powder is an example of a solid-solid _____ mixture.
e: A mixture of flour and rice powder is an example of a solid-solid heterogeneous mixture. A heterogeneous mixture has visibly different parts. Homogeneous would fill a different blank than heterogeneous.

q: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a _____.
e: Filtration is a method for separating an insoluble solid from a liquid. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact. Gas would fill a different blank than liquid.

q: In filtration, the water that passes through the filter paper is called the _____.
e: In filtration, the water that passes through the filter paper is called the filtrate. Filtrate is the idea that completes this fact. Solute would fill a different blank than filtrate.

q: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid _____ state.
e: Crystallisation is defined as a process by which a chemical is converted from a liquid solution into a solid crystalline state. Crystalline is the idea that completes this fact. Amorphous would fill a different blank than crystalline.

q: Decanting is just allowing a mixture of solid and liquid or two immiscible liquids to settle and separate by _____.
e: Decanting is just allowing a mixture of solid and liquid or two immiscible liquids to settle and separate by gravity. Gravity is the idea that completes this fact. Magnetism would fill a different blank than gravity.

q: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different _____ points can be separated.
e: Simple distillation is a procedure by which two liquids with different boiling points can be separated. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point. Melting would fill a different blank than boiling.

q: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a _____ column.
e: Fractional distillation is a method for separation of a liquid mixture into fractions with different boiling points by means of distillation, typically using a fractionating column. A fractionating column lets a liquid mixture split into fractions with different boiling points. Chromatography would fill a different blank than fractionating.

q: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and _____ speed.
e: Centrifugation is a technique used for the separation of particles from a solution according to their size, shape, density, viscosity of the medium and rotor speed. Rotor is the idea that completes this fact. Linear would fill a different blank than rotor.

q: Chromatography is a separation method that depends on the speed at which substances move through special media, consisting of a stationary phase and a _____ phase.
e: Chromatography is a separation method that depends on the speed at which substances move through special media, consisting of a stationary phase and a mobile phase. Mobile is the idea that completes this fact. Liquid would fill a different blank than mobile.

q: An element is a substance that cannot be broken down into other simpler substances through _____ means.
e: An element is a substance that cannot be broken down into other simpler substances through chemical means. Chemical is the idea that completes this fact. Physical would fill a different blank than chemical.

q: Every element is made up of its own type of atoms, therefore it has a unique position in the _____ Table.
e: Every element is made up of its own type of atoms, therefore it has an unique position in the Periodic Table. The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number so similar properties sit in groups. Multiplication would fill a different blank than Periodic.

q: A compound is a substance containing two or more different elements chemically joined together in a fixed _____.
e: A compound is a substance containing two or more different elements chemically joined together in a fixed ratio. Ratio is the idea that completes this fact. State would fill a different blank than ratio.

q: A molecule is the simplest unit of the chemical substance, usually a group of two or more _____.
e: A molecule is the simplest unit of the chemical substance, usually a group of two or more atoms. Atoms is the idea that completes this fact. Electrons would fill a different blank than atoms.

q: Diatomic molecules are molecules composed of only _____ atoms of same or different elements.
e: Diatomic molecules are molecules composed of only two atoms of same or different elements. Two is the idea that completes this fact. Four would fill a different blank than two.

q: Triatomic molecules are molecules composed of only _____ atoms of same or different elements.
e: Triatomic molecules are molecules composed of only three atoms of same or different elements. Three is the idea that completes this fact. Two would fill a different blank than three.

q: Polyatomic molecules are molecules composed of _____ or more atoms of same or different elements.
e: Polyatomic molecules are molecules composed of three or more atoms of same or different elements. Three is the idea that completes this fact. One would fill a different blank than three.
